confirmed.title: Lock-order deadlock between report edits or Run Now and a schedule firing
confirmed.scenario: `update`, `setActive` and `archive` take `FOR UPDATE OF r` on saved_report (reportById {lock:true}) and then write report_schedule (saveSchedule or setScheduleState). `fireSlot` takes `FOR UPDATE OF s` (scheduleToFire) and then inserts home_report_run, whose foreign-key check needs FOR KEY SHARE on the same saved_report row. FOR UPDATE blocks FOR KEY SHARE, so an owner saving or pausing a report at the moment its slot fires deadlocks. Run Now can deadlock the same way: it holds r and waits on the `report_run` numbering_counter row, while fireSlot holds the counter and waits on r. I reproduced the first ordering in a private schema: Postgres answers `40P01 deadlock detected`. Either the person's save gets a 500 or the slot job fails and retries.
confirmed.fix: Lock the report with `FOR NO KEY UPDATE OF r` in reportById, which does not conflict with the foreign key's KEY SHARE. Alternatively, take the schedule row lock before the report lock on every write path.
fixes:
In src/modules/reports/reports.repo.js:134, reportById, change `FOR UPDATE OF r` to `FOR NO KEY UPDATE OF r`.

This is safe because no write to saved_report changes a key column: updateReport and archiveReport only set name, definition, shared, archived_at and updated_at. The weaker lock still makes two writers on the same report take turns, since FOR NO KEY UPDATE conflicts with FOR NO KEY UPDATE, and name claims stay serialised by lockOwner's advisory lock.

What changes is that fireSlot's foreign-key FOR KEY SHARE on the report no longer waits. In the reproduction this removed the deadlock in all five orderings: update with saveSchedule, update with deleteSchedule, setActive, archive, and runNow against the report_run counter. Update the reportById JSDoc ("hold the report") to say the lock does not block runs being inserted against the report.

Give every path the same lock order: report, then schedule, then numbering counter. The minimal change is in fireSlot. In repo.scheduleToFire, before the existing `FOR UPDATE OF s` select, run:

```sql
SELECT 1 FROM saved_report r
  JOIN report_schedule s ON s.saved_report_id = r.saved_report_id
 WHERE s.report_schedule_id = $1
 FOR KEY SHARE OF r
```

`FOR NO KEY UPDATE OF r` in that first statement also works, and it fully serializes the slot with edits. Either way the slot job queues behind an owner's save, pause or archive, and then reads the schedule's new state (paused or archived means skipped). It also never holds the schedule or counter row while waiting for the report.

I reproduced this ordering: the rename plus schedule change against fireSlot then commits on both sides. Changing reportById to `FOR NO KEY UPDATE OF r` is a useful extra but not enough alone, because a rename upgrades the report row lock to FOR UPDATE.

Make `fireSlot` take its locks in the same order as every other write path: report row, then schedule row, then counter.

In `scheduleToFire` (src/modules/reports/reports.repo.js:350), run one statement before the existing `FOR UPDATE OF s` select:

```sql
SELECT 1 FROM saved_report r
  JOIN report_schedule s ON s.saved_report_id = r.saved_report_id
 WHERE s.report_schedule_id = $1
   FOR KEY SHARE OF r
```

It must stay a separate statement because the order of row locks inside one statement is not guaranteed.

A schedule's `saved_report_id` never changes, so the unlocked lookup is safe. If an edit holds the report, the slot job now waits before it holds anything. Under READ COMMITTED it then reads the schedule as the edit committed it, paused or with a new `next_run_at`, and skips as it is meant to.

I tested this against all three cases in the scratch schema, keeping `FOR UPDATE OF r` on the edit side: all completed with no deadlock.

`FOR NO KEY UPDATE OF r` in `reportById` on its own is not enough. A save that renames the report and changes its schedule still deadlocks, because of the `UNIQUE (owner_user_id, name)` constraint.

confirmed.title: Saving a running schedule after its slot is due drops that slot
confirmed.scenario: `scheduleFields` always sets `next_run_at = nextSlot(fields, now)`, strictly after now. `update` uses it for any schedule change, including a recipient-only edit or a formats list sent in a different order. Example: Daily Attendance runs every working day at 18:00 and the worker is down from 17:30 to 19:00. At 18:30 the owner adds a recipient. next_run_at moves to tomorrow at 18:00, and the queued or next-tick job for today's 18:00 slot sees `next_run_at !== slot` and returns "not this slot". Today's report never goes to anyone. home.md §6 says a slot missed while the worker was down is sent once, late.
confirmed.fix: When the schedule stays active and its recurrence, starts_on and run_time are unchanged, keep the stored next_run_at. Otherwise, when the stored next_run_at is already due, compute the next slot from just before it rather than from now.
fixes:
In update(), after the scheduleFields call at line 421, keep a slot that is already due when the schedule stays running:

```js
if (before.report_schedule_id && active && before.next_run_at && new Date(before.next_run_at) <= now) fields.next_run_at = before.next_run_at;
```

The due slot then fires once, late, with the saved recipients and formats, and fireSlot moves the schedule to its next slot after now, as home.md §6 says. Optionally, when the stored next_run_at is still in the future and recurrence, starts_on and run_time are unchanged, keep it too, so a recipient-only edit leaves the time alone. `if (before.report_schedule_id && before.active && before.next_run_at && new Date(before.next_run_at) <= now) fields.next_run_at = before.next_run_at;`

The pending slot then fires once, late, with the newly saved recipients and formats. `fireSlot` then moves the schedule to `nextSlot(s, now)` under the new rule, which is the behaviour home.md §6 describes. This works whether or not recurrence, starts_on or run_time changed, so the suggested "compute from just before it" branch is not needed.

To stop a reordered formats list counting as a change, have `sameSchedule` compare `formats` sorted.

Add an integration test next to "a slot missed while the worker was down": set a due `next_run_at`, PATCH the recipients, and expect `fireSlot(id, due)` to make the slot's runs.

confirmed.title: Run Now can return an old scheduled run once the schedule is removed
confirmed.scenario: `home_report_run.report_schedule_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` (1150), and `update` with `schedule: null` deletes the schedule (service line 429). Its pending runs then have `report_schedule_id` NULL but keep `scheduled_for`. `pendingOnDemand` matches only `report_schedule_id IS NULL AND status = 'pending'`, so it picks them up. Example: an owner is a recipient of a PDF schedule whose run is still pending (PDFs wait for pdf-render, and without Chromium they retry for a long time). The owner switches the report to on demand and presses Run Now (pdf). They get the old scheduled run back, with `requested_by` null. Its file is built `as_at` the old `scheduled_for` (generate.build uses `run.scheduled_for || run.run_at`) rather than now, and the email says `scheduled: false`.
confirmed.fix: Add `AND scheduled_for IS NULL AND requested_by IS NOT NULL` to pendingOnDemand, so only true on-demand runs dedupe a press.
fixes: In pendingOnDemand (src/modules/reports/reports.repo.js:499-501), match only true on-demand runs by also requiring that the run has no slot: `AND report_schedule_id IS NULL AND scheduled_for IS NULL AND status = 'pending'`. `scheduled_for IS NULL` is enough on its own. The 1150 check constraint means every scheduled run has a slot, and the slot survives the FK SET NULL. I checked this against the reproduced state: the current predicate matches the orphan (1 row) and the proposed one does not (0 rows). The suggested `requested_by IS NOT NULL` is redundant: for an on-demand run, requested_by is the same user as recipient_user_id, which is ON DELETE RESTRICT, so it cannot be nulled. A regression test should go in tests/integration/home-reports.test.js: fire a slot, remove the schedule, press Run Now in the same format, and expect a new run with scheduled_for null and requested_by set to the caller.

Add `AND scheduled_for IS NULL` to the WHERE clause of `pendingOnDemand` (reports.repo.js about line 500), so only true on-demand runs dedupe a press:

```sql
WHERE saved_report_id = $1 AND recipient_user_id = $2 AND format = $3
  AND report_schedule_id IS NULL AND scheduled_for IS NULL AND status = 'pending'
```

`scheduled_for` alone is enough. `queueRun` always stores NULL for a Run Now or Export run, and every scheduled run carries its slot (`home_report_run_slot_check`). It also survives `ON DELETE SET NULL`. The suggested `requested_by IS NOT NULL` adds nothing beyond that and can be left out. Optionally, add an integration case to tests/integration/home-reports.test.js: remove a schedule while its run is pending, press Run Now, and expect a new run number.

In `pendingOnDemand` (src/modules/reports/reports.repo.js:500), add `AND scheduled_for IS NULL`, giving `... AND report_schedule_id IS NULL AND scheduled_for IS NULL AND status = 'pending'`. That condition alone is enough. A true on-demand run never has a slot. A scheduled run keeps its slot even after its schedule is deleted, and the CHECK constraint already enforces that a scheduled run has `scheduled_for`.

The extra `requested_by IS NOT NULL` is not needed. `requested_by` is always the recipient for runs on demand, and the recipient's FK is RESTRICT. Leaving it out keeps the filter to one rule.

Optionally, add an integration case to tests/integration/home-reports.test.js: schedule a report with a pending run, PATCH `schedule: null`, press Run Now, and expect a new run with `scheduled_for` null.

confirmed.title: The HOME_STAGING_ROWS deletion steps undo themselves: the manifest is built from the rows the owning milestone is told to remove
confirmed.scenario:
DATABASE_SCHEMA's 'Read by Home' notes (lines 196, 226, 281, 307), home.md §11 (line 660) and the forward-rows.js header (lines 10-11) all tell an owning milestone the same thing. In one PR it must 'delete exactly the ids HOME_STAGING_ROWS lists for these tables' and also 'take those rows out of seeds/staging/lib/forward-rows.js'. But HOME_STAGING_ROWS is computed from ROWS (forward-rows.js:481-489), so once the rows are removed their manifest entries become `ids: []`.

Example with M7: its new 70_partners.js deletes by `require('../staging/60_home').HOME_STAGING_ROWS` for the partner tables, and the same PR removes PARTNERS, OPPORTUNITIES and the rest from forward-rows.js. The delete then removes nothing. The partner rows that earlier staging runs of 60_home wrote stay on staging next to M7's own seed, so the pipeline and signed value are counted twice.

The same steps also break Home's own tests, which the notes never mention:
- tests/unit/home-staging-seed.test.js:85 and :88 fail, because DELETE_ORDER still names the tables but their id lists are empty.
- tests/integration/home-staging-seed.test.js:204 and :257-275 fail, because they expect a partner_inactivity alert and partnership cards above 0 from 60_home alone.

The notes also leave out Home's seeded high-severity alerts (Quiet Partners, Budget Nearly Spent). Their subject_id is the deleted partner or budget id, and nothing ever closes them: alerts.sweeps.js says 'Nothing here clears an alert'. They stay open, are counted in Open High Alerts and link to records that no longer exist.
confirmed.fix: Keep the manifest independent of ROWS. Either freeze every id the seed has ever written in a literal list kept after rows are removed, or tell owners to copy the literal ids into their own seed before deleting the rows. Say in the notes that the same PR must also update DELETE_ORDER and both home-staging-seed tests. Also tell owners to dismiss Home's open alerts whose subject_id is one of the deleted ids.

Stop the manifest depending on rows that are still in the file. Pick one:

(a) **Smallest change, docs only.** Update the forward-rows.js header, home.md §11 and the four DATABASE_SCHEMA notes to say: "the owning milestone's seed deletes the ids as a literal list copied from HOME_STAGING_ROWS (`node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify(require('./seeds/staging/lib/forward-rows').HOME_STAGING_ROWS))"`) before it removes those rows, never by requiring the manifest at runtime. The same PR drops the table from DELETE_ORDER and its expectations from tests/unit/home-staging-seed.test.js and tests/integration/home-staging-seed.test.js."

(b) **Durable.** Add a frozen `RETIRED` list of `{table, key}` to forward-rows.js. The owner moves the rows' keys into it instead of deleting them, and HOME_STAGING_ROWS is built from ROWS plus RETIRED, so a runtime `require` keeps returning the ids.

In either case, add one line telling the owner's seed to also dismiss, through the alerts service, Home's open home_alert rows whose subject_id is one of the ids it deletes.

Make the manifest independent of ROWS. Generate the ids once and pin them as literals, for example in seeds/staging/lib/home-staging-ids.json (or a literal frozen array in forward-rows.js) shaped `{ table, id_column, ids }` in DELETE_ORDER. Build HOME_STAGING_ROWS from that pinned list, not from ROWS. In tests/unit/home-staging-seed.test.js, replace the equality check at :86-88 with a subset check: every ROWS id must appear in the pinned list. Removing rows then keeps their ids in the manifest. Optionally, 60_home can delete pinned ids that no longer have a row, so retired rows clean themselves up.

Then change the owner notes (DATABASE_SCHEMA.md :196-200, :226-229, :281-285, :307-310, home.md §11 :658-661 and the forward-rows.js header). The owning PR deletes the pinned ids for its tables, removes the rows from ROWS, keeps the ids in the pinned list, and updates the home-staging-seed tests that expect figures from those tables. It also dismisses Home's open seeded alerts whose subject_id is a deleted id.

If code is not to change in this PR, the minimal fix is the docs alone: tell the owner to copy the literal ids from HOME_STAGING_ROWS into its own seed before removing the rows, since the manifest is derived from ROWS and empties when they go.

confirmed.scenario:
The file takes about 19 s and reads the real clock throughout. Three narrow windows make `npm run ci` fail depending on when it starts:

1. Monday 08:00 Lagos. 'Leave Requests' (lines 418-426) is a weekly Monday 08:00 schedule starting today. If the file starts on a Monday shortly before 08:00:00 Lagos, that schedule becomes due partway through. The tick at line 816 then returns {due: 2} with two queued jobs instead of {due: 1} and one job, and `queueDue()` at lines 869 and 1062 returns {due: 1} instead of {due: 0}.
2. Lagos midnight. The attendance_day rows are written for `today`, taken once at line 197. The manager's XLSX is gathered for `lagos.today(run.run_at)`, which is the moment Run Now is pressed a few seconds later. Crossing midnight in between empties the file, so line 639's `['Musa Danjuma']` fails.
3. Month start. Line 1033 counts runs from the month of the `today` taken in beforeAll, while the service's runs_this_month uses the month at call time. A run crossing a month boundary in Lagos makes line 1038 fail.

Each window is short, but these are exactly the day and time boundaries the gate is supposed to be deterministic across.
confirmed.fix: Remove the dependence on the real clock in the time-sensitive parts. Give the weekly report a start date it cannot reach during the run, for example `starts_on: lagos.addDays(today, 14)`. Insert the late and present attendance_day rows for `lagos.today(new Date(runs.managerXlsx.run_at))`, the day the run actually reads, rather than the `today` from beforeAll. Compute the month in `done()` at the moment the summary is asked for, not from beforeAll's `today`.
